claim: AlphaAgent (LLM-driven formulaic alpha mining with complexity/hypothesis-alignment/novelty regularization) is evaluated on Qlib OHLCV-only price-volume factors on both China CSI 500 and U.S. S&P 500, test split spanning 2021-2025 (prose: Jan 2021-Dec 2024). Table 2 results (test window): CSI 500 IC 0.0212, ICIR 0.1938, annualized excess return 11.00%, IR 1.488, MDD -9.36%; S&P 500 IC 0.0056, ICIR 0.0552, annualized excess return 8.74%, IR 1.0545, MDD -9.10%. The S&P 500 IC (0.0056) is roughly a quarter of the CSI 500 IC (0.0212) for the identical method and identical LLM backend, i.e. the same LLM-driven formulaic-alpha loop generalizes far more weakly to U.S. equities than to China A-shares.
quote: our framework achieves an average annual excess return of 11.0% (IR=1.5) and 8.74% (IR=1.05) respectively after accounting for transaction costs
market_and_period: China CSI 500 and U.S. S&P 500, Qlib framework, OHLCV-only inputs, train 2015-01/2019-12, validation 2020, test 2021-01/2025-01 (prose describes the window as Jan 2021-Dec 2024).
applicability: Direct primary-source evidence for T-15's prior-art check: the same LLM-hypothesis-to-formula-to-IC-feedback loop this task is testing has already been run on U.S. large/mid-cap equities (S&P 500) with a real, disclosed, non-cherry-picked OOS IC (0.0056) that is an order of magnitude below textbook-anomaly IC and about a quarter of the same method's own China-market IC -- sets a realistic expectation band for what a from-scratch Claude-authored batch should be judged against, not the more impressive CSI 500 number.
limitations: KDD 2025 peer-reviewed paper but GPT-3.5-turbo backend (weaker than current-generation models); test window (2021-2025) only partially overlaps our TEST window (2024-2026) and is not broken out separately for 2023+ only; S&P 500 data from Yahoo Finance (not point-in-time survivorship-bias-free); transaction cost model differs from our 10/20bp per-side convention (0.05% one-side only, no buy-side fee disclosed for the U.S. leg).
independent_replication: No independent third-party replication found (paper is from 2025); code released at github.com/RndmVariableQ/AlphaAgent per the paper text but not independently re-run by us this pass.
impact_on_spec: Sets the realistic U.S.-equity IC expectation band (order 0.005-0.01, not the 0.02+ seen on China A-shares) for judging whether this round's Claude-authored factor batch is worth adopting as a standing method, and confirms the loop pattern (not the RL/GFlowNet search this box cannot run) is the executable, already-precedented mechanism.

claim: R&D-Agent(Q) (Microsoft, NeurIPS 2025) reports an out-of-sample generalizability extension beyond its primary CSI 300 (China) experiment to CSI 500 (China) and NASDAQ 100 (U.S.), with train 2008-01/2021-12, validation 2022-01/2023-12, test 2024-01/2025-06-30 -- a genuine post-2023, LLM-cutoff-safe, U.S.-equity OOS window. NASDAQ 100 test-window results (o4-mini backend): R&D-Agent(Q) IC 0.0162, ICIR 0.1035, IR(Sharpe) 1.7737, MDD -0.0634, versus classical factor libraries on the same universe/window: Alpha158 IC 0.0040, Alpha360 IC 0.0042, AutoAlpha IC 0.0046 -- roughly 3.5-4x the factor-library IC on the identical post-2023 U.S. universe.
quote: using the period from January 1, 2008, to December 31, 2021, for training, January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2023, for validation, and January 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, for testing
market_and_period: NASDAQ 100 (U.S. large-cap tech-heavy), train 2008-2021, validation 2022-2023, test 2024-01 to 2025-06-30.
applicability: The strongest single piece of prior-art evidence found for this task: the same class of method (LLM-driven hypothesis -> factor/model code -> backtest feedback loop, the direction this task adopts as dir:llm_hypothesis_code_backtest_loop) already shows a genuine post-2023 U.S.-equity IC edge over classical factor libraries (Alpha158/Alpha360/AutoAlpha) of roughly 3.5-4x on NASDAQ 100 -- directly on point for the queue task's question (does an LLM-driven factor loop beat an existing factor zoo on IC, on recent US data).
limitations: NASDAQ 100 is a narrow, tech-concentrated 100-name large-cap universe, not the broad top-1000 universe this task uses; o4-mini/GPT-4o backends and a full Research+Development+Feedback multi-agent system (bandit-scheduled hypothesis search across many iterations) are a materially heavier loop than this task's single-pass 8+4-factor preregistered batch; no disclosed trading-cost model for the IC numbers (IC is a pre-cost predictive-power statistic, not a costed book Sharpe).
independent_replication: No independent third-party replication of the NASDAQ100 extension found (paper is 2025, NeurIPS poster); code released at github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent but the NASDAQ100 experiment's exact config was not independently re-run by us this pass.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the adopted loop pattern (dir:llm_hypothesis_code_backtest_loop) has independently-published, post-2023, U.S.-equity, IC-based evidence of beating a classical factor library -- the closest existing precedent to this task's own decision rule (batch's SELECT-chosen factor vs zoo's SELECT-chosen factor on TEST rank IC), used to calibrate expectations rather than copied as a target.

claim: Alpha-GPT (EMNLP 2025 System Demonstration Track) proposes a human-AI interactive alpha-mining paradigm: an LLM-based prompt-engineering framework that converts natural-language research ideas into formulaic alphas, which are then refined/backtested via genetic programming; the system demonstration paper does not disclose a standalone post-2023 U.S.-equity out-of-sample IC/Sharpe table in its abstract-level description.
quote: outputs creative, insightful, and effective alphas
market_and_period: Not disclosed at the abstract level; original 2023 version reports experiments on US stock data 2012-2021 per secondary summaries (not independently verified from the abstract snapshot alone).
applicability: One of the three named methods (Alpha-GPT, AlphaAgent, RD-Agent-Quant) this task's brief asked to check; included for completeness of the prior-art sweep, but contributes no usable post-2023 U.S. decay-evidence number (unlike AlphaAgent and RD-Agent(Q)) -- the abstract-only snapshot means this source is used only to confirm the method exists and its general shape (human-in-the-loop LLM alpha proposal, not an autonomous batch), not for any performance claim.
limitations: Only the abstract page was fetched (full PDF not opened this pass); this is a system-demonstration paper, not a primary results paper with a disclosed OOS test window comparable to the other two sources; no IC/Sharpe numbers extracted.
independent_replication: Not assessed this pass (no performance claim was extracted to replicate).
impact_on_spec: Completes the brief's requested 2-3-source sweep (Alpha-GPT, AlphaAgent, RD-Agent-Quant); confirms Alpha-GPT is a human-in-the-loop interactive tool rather than an autonomous batch process, so it is not a closer analog to this task's method than RD-Agent(Q) or AlphaAgent.

claim: Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski (2012, Journal of Finance 67(3):1009-1043) show that over half of insider trades are predictable 'routine' trades with no information content; the remaining 'opportunistic' trades carry all the predictive power in the insider-trading universe, with a value-weighted opportunistic-only portfolio earning 82bp/month abnormal return versus essentially zero for routine trades.
quote: there is predictable, identifiable "routine" insider trading that is not informative for the future of firms
market_and_period: US insider (Form 4) filings, NBER working paper / Journal of Finance 2012 published version.
applicability: Grounds candidate F2 (opportunistic_insider_signal): the project's existing insider_cluster_buy card uses a simple buyer-count>=2 event rule and does not isolate opportunistic vs routine trades; this factor uses insider_broad's own opportunistic_buy_60d/routine_buy_60d columns to directly operationalize this paper's key distinction, a new element versus the already-tested standalone insider-cluster mechanism.
limitations: Original classification used SEC Form 4 role/history heuristics on CRSP/Compustat-linked data over a different sample period (late 1980s-2000s); our insider_broad store's own opportunistic/routine classification logic was not independently re-derived or audited against the paper's exact algorithm this pass.
independent_replication: Widely cited (1000+ citations), one of the most replicated results in the insider-trading literature.
impact_on_spec: Fixes F2's exact construction (opportunistic minus routine insider buy activity) before any IC is computed.

claim: Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin (2001, Journal of Finance 56(3):877-919) find that stocks experiencing unusually high (low) trading volume over a day or a week tend to appreciate (depreciate) over the following month, consistent with trading-activity shocks raising a stock's visibility and subsequent demand.
quote: stocks experiencing unusually high (low) trading volume over a day or a week tend to appreciate (depreciate) over the course of the following month
market_and_period: US equities (NYSE/AMEX), sample ending in the 1990s.
applicability: Grounds candidate F3 (trading_activity_surge): trade_count_5d_mean/trade_count_21d_mean from daily_broad is an unused-elsewhere ratio proxying a recent participation surge relative to baseline, distinct from dollar-volume-level controls already in the project (dollar_adv_21/63) and distinct from the refuted overnight/intraday return-decomposition cards (this factor uses transaction COUNT, not return decomposition).
limitations: Original paper's volume measure is share/dollar volume, not transaction count; the two are correlated but not identical (transaction count also reflects order fragmentation/algorithmic activity that grew hugely post-2001), so this is an adaptation, not a direct replication.
independent_replication: Widely cited (the 'high-volume return premium' is a standard reference point in the trading-activity/attention literature; Kaniel-Li-Starks later extended it internationally).
impact_on_spec: Fixes F3's exact construction (recent-vs-baseline trade-count ratio) and sign (long the surge) before any IC is computed.

claim: Christophe, Ferri and Hsieh (2010, Journal of Financial Economics 95(1):85-106) find abnormal short-selling in the three days before 670 Nasdaq analyst downgrades (2000-2001), significantly related to the subsequent price reaction, consistent with short sellers being informed traders.
quote: We find abnormal levels of short-selling in the three days before downgrades are publicly announced
applicability: Supports F1's premise (short sellers are informed traders, so a fall in short interest alongside insider buying is a convergence of two independently-informed signals, not noise) and F4/F6's premise (short-volume pressure carries information about near-term price direction).
limitations: Sample is downgrade-specific and pre-Reg SHO (2000-2001); short-selling institutional mechanics have changed materially since (Reg SHO, post-2008 short-sale rules, FINRA short-volume public disclosure which our short_volume_broad store itself relies on).
independent_replication: Cited widely in the informed-short-selling literature; consistent with Diether/Lee/Werner (2009) and Boehmer/Jones/Zhang (2008) on informed short-selling.
impact_on_spec: Supports the informed-short-seller premise used by F1, F4 and F6 before any IC is computed.

claim: Diether, Lee and Werner (2009, Review of Financial Studies 22(2):575-607) show short sellers increase trading following positive returns and correctly predict future negative abnormal returns, using 2005 SEC-mandated short-sale data; short sales were 24% of NYSE and 31% of Nasdaq share volume.
quote: Short sellers increase their trading following positive returns and they correctly predict future negative abnormal returns
market_and_period: US equities (NYSE and Nasdaq), 2005 SEC pilot short-sale data.
applicability: Grounds F4 (SUE + short-volume gate) and F6 (momentum + short-volume gate): short sellers trade on short-term overreaction, so elevated short-volume pressure against a positive-SUE or momentum stock signals informed disagreement, while its absence is a confirming signal.
limitations: 2005 pilot-program sample predates our short_volume_broad store's own FINRA-based short-volume-ratio construction (which starts 2018-08 in our data); short-selling regulatory regime (Reg SHO uptick-rule repeal in 2007, etc.) differs across periods.
independent_replication: Widely cited; consistent with the broader short-sale-constraint literature (Diamond & Verrecchia 1987; Boehmer, Jones & Zhang 2008).
impact_on_spec: Supports the informed-short-seller-as-confirming/disagreeing-signal premise used by F4 and F6 before any IC is computed.

claim: Chordia, Subrahmanyam and Anshuman (2001, Journal of Financial Economics 59(1):3-32) document a negative cross-sectional relation between expected stock returns and the VARIABILITY of trading activity (dollar volume / share turnover), after controlling for size, book-to-market, momentum and the level of volume/turnover.
quote: Trading Activity and Expected Stock Returns
applicability: Secondary support for F3's use of a trading-activity ratio (rather than a raw level, which is already a control via dollar_adv) as the informative construct; distinguishes the level-of-activity premium (Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin, used as the primary citation) from the variability-of-activity discount this paper documents, both pointing to trading-activity dynamics (not just level) carrying return-relevant information.
limitations: Abstract/title-only confirmation this pass (RePEc landing page did not surface the full abstract text; bibliographic facts -- authors, journal, volume, pages, year -- were independently confirmed via web search of multiple citing sources, not full-text read).
independent_replication: Standard reference in the liquidity/trading-activity asset-pricing literature; over 1000 citations.
impact_on_spec: Secondary support only; does not by itself fix any formula parameter.

claim: Ke, Huddart and Petroni (2003, Journal of Accounting and Economics 35(3):315-346) find insiders trade on knowledge of specific forthcoming accounting disclosures up to two years ahead; insider stock sales increase three to nine quarters before a break in a string of consecutive quarterly earnings increases.
quote: What insiders know about future earnings and how they use it
market_and_period: US equities, insider Form 4 filings linked to quarterly earnings histories.
applicability: Grounds F8 (earnings-recency-gated insider buying): insiders' information advantage is sharpest around earnings disclosures, so gating insider net-buying to the window shortly after a fundamentals report isolates the freshest-information trades, a new element versus unconditional insider buying.
limitations: Abstract/title-only confirmation this pass (RePEc landing page did not surface the full abstract text; bibliographic facts confirmed via web search of multiple citing sources, not full-text read); the paper's own focus is insider SELLING ahead of earnings declines, not buying after positive reports -- the buying-side, post-report-window application here is our own extrapolation from the general 'insiders trade on private knowledge of near-term earnings trajectory' finding, not a literal restatement of the paper's own tested direction.
independent_replication: Widely cited in the insider-trading/earnings-informativeness literature.
impact_on_spec: Supports F8's construction; the limitation above is a real one-sided extrapolation and is why F8's confidence is set at 0.50, not higher.
